proposed.sourceName: Darul Iftaa Mahmudiyyah (Lusaka, Zambia) — Fatwa #326 on Glycerine
proposed.paraphrase: Plant and synthetic glycerine is permissible, but glycerine obtained from an animal source is not permissible since the fat is generally derived from a non-halal animal; one should check the source of the glycerine before use and exercise caution when it is unverified.

proposed.sourceName: Islam Q&A — Fatwa 97541 (citing the Standing Committee for Issuing Fatwas)
proposed.paraphrase: Glycerine from pigs or from animals not slaughtered Islamically is haram — one may not eat, drink or use it when haram content is certain or strongly likely — and is permissible only when from a lawfully and properly slaughtered animal (an istihalah exception applies where the fat is chemically transformed into a genuinely different substance).

researcherNote: E422 seeded zabiha = grade 4 (Questionable — widely avoided). Glycerol of unknown source could be non-zabiha animal fat or pork; both tier-1 Sunni fatwas require a lawfully-slaughtered source / verification, so the strict zabiha position avoids unverified E422. Two independent tier-1 sources. APPROVED by owner 2026-07-01.
